newsitem.title: USA: Clinton names Thurman director of AIDS office.
newsitem.headline: Clinton names Thurman director of AIDS office.

text.p: President Clinton Monday named Sandra Thurman director of the Office of National AIDS Policy, which coordinates federal policy and programmes to combat the disease, the White House said in a statement.

Thurman worked on The Task Force for Child Survival and Development at Atlanta's Carter Centre from 1993 to 1996 and as Executive Director of AID Atlanta, which provides health and support services to people with HIV and AIDS, 1988-1993.
AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) is caused by HIV (Human Immuno-deficiency Virus) and attacks the body's immune system. There is no known cure for the disease.

The AIDS activist group ACT UP leaked news of the announcement Sunday and a spokesman for the organisation, Wayne Turner, denounced Thurman as the fourth in a series of "ineffective, no-name bureacrats" named to the position.

AIDS activists have been pressing Clinton to name a more senior official and to upgrade the position to one with a seat in Clinton's cabinet. Thurman will replace Eric Goosby, who succeeded Patsy Fleming and Kristine Gebbie in the position.
